players.product: AI/automotive chip designer - Samsung Foundry contract-manufacturing customer (USD 16.5B, 2025-2033)

quarterly_data.signal: TerraFab proposed as the answer to a chip-supply ceiling ('I mentioned this at the shareholder meeting'): Musk said the limiting factor for Tesla growth 'three or four years out, I think it actually is chip production. Is there enough AI logic and enough memory, enough RAM for volume?' Even the best-case output of Tesla's key suppliers - 'strategic partners like Samsung, TSMC, and Micron' - is not enough ('Then it's not enough.'), so 'we're going to have to build a Tesla TerraFab, a very big fab that includes logic, memory, and packaging. Domestically.' He added that 'maybe memory is an even bigger limiter than AI logic' because 'currently, there are no advanced memory fabs at scale in the United States', cited protection against geopolitical risk, and said 'We'll have a bigger announcement on this in the future.' The chip fab is not included in the 2026 capex outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (chip supply seen as the growth limiter three or four years out)

quarterly_data.signal: AI chip roadmap: Musk called completing the AI5 chip design 'arguably the number one most critical thing to get done' (he spends 'pretty much every Saturday on this, and a chunk of every Tuesday') and is 'quite confident about the design at this point'. AI6 'aspirationally would follow that in under a year' and will be 'yet another big leap beyond AI5'. Tesla will use AI5 chips in its data centers ('We already use the AI4 chips in our data centers'); 'When we do training, it's a combination of the AI4 chips and NVIDIA hardware.' No external chip sales for now: 'we first need to make sure we have enough chips for our vehicle production, all of our Optimus production.'
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (AI6 aspirationally in under a year after AI5)

quarterly_data.signal: Memory and logic supply outlook (asked about tight memory supply): Musk said 'we do have a solution for logic and memory for, let's say, the next roughly three years', but beyond that 'we will be supplier limited and so we've got to figure out some game plan to not be supplier limited' - hence the push for more US fab capacity given geopolitical uncertainty, since 'Optimus is completely useless without an AI chip'. He argued Tesla's AI is 'more than an order of magnitude better' in memory efficiency ('intelligence per gigabyte') than the big models, which helps it scale under RAM constraints.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (logic and memory solution for the next roughly three years)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 capex outlook (CFO Vaibhav Taneja): 2025 capex ended 'slightly below our previous guidance of $9 billion'; 2026 capex is expected 'in excess of $20 billion', paying for six factories ('the refinery, LFP factories, CyberCab, Semi, a new mega factory, the Optimus factory') plus 'building our AI compute infrastructure' (scaling Optimus means 'we need a lot more compute', including for training) and more capacity at existing factories. The $20 billion does NOT include the solar cell fab or 'the semiconductor chip fab', which are 'infrastructure plays' coming later and may be funded with more debt or other means. Near-term funding comes from 'over $44 billion of cash and investments'; for the robotaxi fleet, 'We have had conversations with banks about it.' Free cash flow ended at $1.4 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx in excess of $20 billion (excludes solar and chip fabs); 2025 CapEx slightly below previous guidance of $9 billion; over $44 billion of cash and investments; free cash flow $1.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results color (CFO): total gross margin 'over 20.1%, something which we haven't achieved for over the last two years'; automotive margins excluding credits improved sequentially 'from 15.4% to 17.9%', with automotive gross profit flat despite '16% lower deliveries'; FSD reached 'nearly 1,100,000 paid customers globally' ('nearly 70% were upfront purchases'), and Tesla is moving fully to a subscription-based FSD model from this quarter; operating expenses rose $500 million sequentially, and spend on AI-related initiatives and new products stays elevated through 2026. 'We therefore ended 2025 with a bigger backlog than in recent years.' 'Our biggest constraint globally continues to be on the battery pack front.'
quarterly_data.figure: total gross margin over 20.1%; automotive margin excluding credits from 15.4% to 17.9%; nearly 1,100,000 paid FSD customers (nearly 70% upfront purchases)

quarterly_data.signal: Energy (CFO): record storage deployments and record energy gross profit in Q4; the energy business ended 2025 with 'nearly $12.8 billion in revenue, a 26.6% year-over-year growth' on demand for both MegaPack and Powerwall. For 2026 'our backlog remains strong, well-diversified globally', with rising deployments expected from the launch of 'MegaPack 3 and Mega Block', but margin compression is expected from low-cost competition, policy uncertainty and tariffs. Musk: Tesla is building more energy manufacturing capacity and will 'work towards getting 100 gigawatts a year of solar cell production', integrated from raw materials to finished solar panels.
quarterly_data.figure: energy revenue nearly $12.8 billion in 2025, a 26.6% year-over-year growth; solar cell production goal of 100 gigawatts a year

quarterly_data.signal: Optimus (an AI chip end market): Tesla will wind down Model S and X production next quarter and convert that Fremont space into an Optimus factory, with 'a long-term goal of having a million units a year of Optimus robots'. Optimus 3 will probably be unveiled in a few months. Because 'it is a completely new supply chain, there's really nothing from the existing supply chains that exist in Optimus', so 'It will be a stretched-out S curve'. Optimus is still in the R&D phase, with no significant production volume 'until probably the end of this year'. Musk: 'Optimus won't even be able to just sit there without an AI chip.'
quarterly_data.figure: long-term goal of a million units a year of Optimus in Fremont

quarterly_data.signal: Robotaxi / Cybercab (demand for AI4-equipped vehicles): paid robotaxi rides with no safety monitor have started in Austin. Musk: 'we're well over 500' taxi vehicles carrying paid customers between the Bay Area and Austin, likely to 'double every month type of thing'. Cybercab (no steering wheel or pedals) is expected to 'start production in April', and Tesla expects fully autonomous vehicles in 'somewhere between a quarter and half of the United States by the end of the year', pending regulatory approval. Musk noted 'we have millions of cars with AI4' that owners could add to the autonomous fleet.
quarterly_data.figure: well over 500 paid robotaxi vehicles (Bay Area and Austin); Cybercab production start in April
